note: Selective CRTH2/DP2 antagonists (OC000459, BI 671800, QAV680/fevipiprant, setipiprant) in seasonal allergic rhinitis: allergen-chamber studies were positive, the one field Phase 3 (setipiprant) failed, and none reached the market.
label: Allergic rhinitis (CRTH2)

engagement.model: Human whole-blood PGD2 eosinophil shape-change assay
engagement.note: Class compounds were optimised on PGD2-induced eosinophil shape change in human whole blood; no patient-side comparison yet.
engagement.quote: The activities of the compounds were evaluated in a human DP2 binding assay and a human whole blood eosinophil shape change assay.
engagement.judgement: Earliest class use found of the assay that later served OC000459 (Pettipher 2012, whole-blood pKB 7.5) and the rest of the class; the 2009 compounds are class proxies, not the clinical candidates.

engagement.model: Human whole-blood PGD2 eosinophil shape-change assay
engagement.note: BI 671800 gave a dose-related fall in ex vivo PGD2-induced eosinophil shape change in chamber-challenged SAR patients, as the assay said.
engagement.quote: induced a dose-related reduction in ex vivo prostaglandin D2-mediated eosinophil shape change
engagement.reason: Ex vivo shape change blocked dose-dependently
engagement.judgement: Same assay run in vitro (model) and ex vivo on patient blood in NCT01007721 (146 SAR patients, Fraunhofer chamber; no results posted). Abstract only (JACI paywalled); the quote is a verbatim fragment of a 45-word sentence. The paper reports the patient readout without putting the in vitro potency beside it, so comparison_stated is false; product_in_model is null because no preclinical BI 671800 shape-change paper was found.

dose.note: Occupancy modelling put <30% of subjects at >=90% trough CRTH2 blockade on the 1000 mg b.i.d. dose; invoked post hoc, never tested prospectively.
dose.short: Occupancy model invoked post hoc only
dose.quote: the median percentage of subjects with at least 90% CRTH2 blockage at trough plasma setipiprant concentrations was higher with 1000 mg b.i.d. than with 500 mg b.i.d. doses, but still remained below 30%
dose.judgement: The Phase 3 dose (1000 mg b.i.d.) was actually chosen from an asthma bronchial allergen-challenge proof-of-mechanism study (belongs to the asthma/CRTH2 draft), not from a rhinitis model. Ratner cites the occupancy modelling only to explain the Phase 3 null after the fact ('borderline efficacy'), so it is a post hoc rationalisation, not a prediction that was tested; left untested rather than same. Quote is a verbatim fragment of a >40-word sentence. model_first_use_year is the earliest source I verified; the underlying modelling paper was not chased.

efficacy.model: OVA-sensitised mouse allergic rhinitis (sneezing, nasal rubs, nasal obstruction)
efficacy.note: Selective DP2 antagonists (tricyclic series; AM156 in 2010) relieved sneezing and nasal rubs in sensitised mice; none of the clinical candidates was reported in it.
efficacy.short: DP2 antagonists work in mouse rhinitis
efficacy.quote: The lead compound was demonstrated to have efficacy in a mouse model of allergic rhinitis following oral dosing.
efficacy.judgement: Mouse rhinitis model was used only for class proxies (Stearns 2009 tricyclics; Stebbins 2010 AM156, doi 10.1016/j.ejphar.2010.04.031; Shiraishi 2014 ARRY-063, doi 10.1111/cea.12280). The pivotal papers for the named drugs did not use it: OC000459 (Pettipher 2012, doi 10.1124/jpet.111.187203) used rat/guinea-pig DK-PGD2 eosinophilia; setipiprant (Fretz 2013, doi 10.1021/jm400122f) reported in vitro potency and rat/dog PK only. The class relied on the human allergen chamber for rhinitis efficacy, hence the model switch in the next entry.

efficacy.model: Human allergen-challenge chamber (Vienna Challenge Chamber, grass pollen)
efficacy.note: OC000459 200 mg b.i.d. cut nasal and ocular symptoms in 35 grass-allergic men over 6 h pollen exposure; no field trial followed.
efficacy.short: OC000459 relieves symptoms in Vienna chamber
efficacy.quote: Treatment with OC000459 was well tolerated and led to a significant and persistent reduction in the symptoms of rhinoconjunctivitis.
efficacy.judgement: Abstract only (Allergy paywalled). Trial NCT01448902 started 2007-03 (no results posted), which opens the chamber's use for the class; a 120-subject dose-finding chamber study (NCT00697281, 2008) is unpublished. BI 671800 repeated the chamber result in the Fraunhofer ECC (Krug 2014: TNSS AUC -17% at 200 mg b.i.d., NCT01007721) and QAV680/QAW039 ran three Novartis EEC studies (NCT00784732, NCT01103050, NCT01804400) with no publication or posted results found. No chamber-tested drug of the class ever had a published field trial in rhinitis.

efficacy.note: Chamber-positive class; setipiprant's 630-patient field Phase 3 found no effect on nasal symptoms (-0.02) while cetirizine worked; Phase 2 had shown -0.15.
efficacy.quote: Setipiprant 1000 mg b.i.d. had no significant effect on this endpoint in the Phase 3 trial (−0.02 [95% CI −0.12, 0.07]; p = 0.652).
efficacy.reason: Field Phase 3 failed; chamber said yes
efficacy.judgement: Called contra because the allergen chamber predicted class efficacy and the only adequately powered field Phase 3 of a selective CRTH2 antagonist in SAR (NCT01484119, n=630, no results posted) found none on the primary or any secondary endpoint while cetirizine was positive. Caveats: setipiprant was never run in the rhinitis chamber (product_in_model false; the chamber tested OC000459, BI 671800, QAV680); the source puts the chamber trials beside only its Phase 2 result ('This is in line with the growing clinical evidence from several CRHT2 antagonists investigated in allergen challenge trials...'), calls the Phase 3 reasons 'not fully known' and offers lower trough exposure, <30% of subjects at >=90% occupancy and a borderline dose, never the model, so comparison_stated is false and source_calls_it null. Alternative readings a re-scorer may prefer: same on the Phase 2 primary (-0.15, 95% CI -0.29 to -0.01, p=0.030, NCT01241214, n=579) or untested if a same-drug chamber-vs-field comparison is required. Full text read (open access, PMC5379543).
